The worker's recorded Probe A/B results ('Expected: Fenced / Actual: Completed' and 'Expected: 2 / Actual: 3') are exactly consistent with this trace and both probes were reported reverted. The production stop branch at LibraryReconciliationService.cs:245-261 is intact with no probe residue (no debug markers; the Overflow-or-Stopped clause present at line 253-254; covered++/lastCovered bookkeeping after the break at lines 264-268). No production change was required, matching the attempt-1 review expectation.

findings.summary: Unchanged from attempt 1: the cursor is a Cache record not exempt from render-cache TTL pruning; default-safe, deferred to 19.5.
findings.detail: Re-verified the production files carrying this interaction are untouched by the rework and the disposition is unchanged. ReconciliationCursorStore writes the cursor under StateAuthority.Cache (ReconciliationCursorStore.cs:132); StateRetentionService.RunRetentionPass exempts only MetadataStateStore.RecordKind (StateRetentionService.cs:147), so the cursor is subject to render-cache age pruning. Under the defaults (RenderCacheTtlMinutes 24h, ArrTagsReconciliationTask.DefaultInterval 12h) the cursor is rewritten before expiry, so the record survives; only an effective whole-scope interval longer than the configured TTL prunes it, causing a bounded restart-from-the-start, which is consistent with ADR-022's Cache 'missing resets to the start' semantics. Deferred to 19.2/19.5 integration verification as recorded in the attempt-1 report.

findings.area: Concurrency / state consistency of the persisted cursor
findings.summary: Unchanged from attempt 1: overlapping whole-scope runs can cause a bounded re-cover but cannot skip an uncovered item.
findings.detail: Re-confirmed the production advance logic is unchanged by the rework: LibraryReconciliationService is a singleton with no cross-run lock; each run reads the cursor once at start and AdvanceCursor persists only the position of the item that run covered. If two runs overlap, the last writer can move the cursor back to an earlier covered position but never forward past an item neither run covered, so the next run re-covers the overlap. Bounded extra work, not a state-integrity failure; no action required.
evidence: src/ArrTags/Reconciliation/LibraryReconciliationService.cs:170,418-437 (single cursor read per run; AdvanceCursor writes only the run's own covered position)
